lesson.title: W-ring tiny selected-policy gain coexists with negative equal-depth mechanism contrast

comparators: actual LOCAL PW36 selected s4s5hz KS7

observations.statement: Split versus actual selected PW36 is positive in both local F1 and paired estimators; gain is tiny and not robustness or transfer evidence.
Equal-depth independent full barriers plus40Bmetadata regress coupled at this configuration in both estimators.
Split versus coupled reverses sign between F1 and paired; depth/footprint and barrier changes are coupled.
Actual incumbent and coupled share exact main instruction stream yet show estimator-dependent context gap.
Split beats equal in both estimators but changes both ring depths and shared-memory footprint.

hypotheses.statement: Barrier separation alone may add synchronization/address cost at equal depth; depth rebalance might compensate, while pointer/allocation/capture context or order may explain some tiny gaps. These causal explanations remain unproven.

lesson.scope: QKV M128/N2304/K8192/KS7 complete single-main graphs on local H100. Equal-minus-coupled tests independent full barriers plus40Bmetadata at equal5/5depth. Split-minus-equal changes both depths and shared footprint. Actual-policy and mechanism contrasts are separate facts.
transfer_limits: No H100-to-H200, component-to-whole-score, cross-run minimum or historicalgain addition.
No automatic serving selection/integration from fixed-arm graph timings; original prepare selection and budget remain separate gates.
Exact same main stream does not guarantee identical allocation/cache/capture context; no causal or robustness claim from32pairs.
Protocol is bounded two-WG source model with finite engine progress; archived output/counter arrays and SO are not retained for independent rerun.
lesson.falsification: The selected-policy hypothesis weakens if split gains disappear/reverse under matched context and alternating order, or identical-main incumbent/coupled controls retain a systematic gap sufficient to explain the observation.

next_test.question: Does split retain a signed gain over actual selected PW36 after matching fixed-arm pointer/allocation roles and diagnosing identical-main control context?
controls: coupledX5W5 and identical-main comparator with matched pointer roles
next_test.discriminator: Predeclare balanced same-fixture complete-graph timing with swapped matched pointer/allocation roles; retain identical-main context gap and all six causal contrasts, then compare split sign versus actual policy and coupled separately.
next_test.stop_rule: Abort validity failure without timing admission; retain every tiny signed contrast and estimator conflict. A persistent same-main context gap requires harness diagnosis before attributing a mechanism win; no family retirement.
required_gates: new frozen reviewed source if harness changes
exact actual JIT/graph identity and selected no-fallback policy
all raw balanced timing samples and cleanup

conditions: A separately admitted matched-context confirmation distinguishes mechanism from policy/context effects.
No extrapolated score or attainable speed gain is known.

cost.basis: Future matched-context source/review/runtime cost unknown; prior trial hardcaps240sinner/300souter are not a new reservation.
